title: Rahab (Joshua 2; 6)
hookLine: a woman on the wall hides the spies and hangs a scarlet cord; she's named in Jesus's family tree
tomorrow: as for me and my house

lines: THE KING'S MEN AT THE DOOR.
cards: Remember the spies who came back saying we were like grasshoppers? A generation later, Joshua sends two more, across the Jordan to Jericho.
They go to a house built right into the city wall, the house of a woman named Rahab. The Bible doesn't soften what she is: a prostitute.
Someone tells the king, and his men come pounding on her door: bring out the men who came to you. She has maybe a minute to decide.
And what she tells the spies afterward would have stunned that first generation: the terror of you has fallen on all of us. Our hearts melted.

teach.h: HIDDEN UNDER FLAX ON THE ROOF.
teach.b: First, the lie and the roof. Rahab has hidden the men under stalks of flax on her roof. She tells the king's men: yes, they came, but they left at dusk; hurry and you'll catch them.
The soldiers run off toward the river. Second, her confession. On the roof, she tells the spies: we heard how the Lord dried up the sea for you.

teach.h: GOD IN HEAVEN ABOVE, EARTH BENEATH.
teach.b: Then a line of faith from someone with every reason not to have it: the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath.
She asks one thing: when you come, spare my father, my mother, my brothers and sisters. Third, the cord. She lets them down through her window on a rope.

They tell her: tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window, and keep your family inside. When Jericho falls, the text says, Joshua spares Rahab and all her family, and she lives in Israel from then on.
Some readers notice that the Hebrew word for this cord, tikvah, is the word used elsewhere for hope: a thread of hope hanging from a window.
Saint Clement of Rome, in his letter to the Corinthians, saw in that scarlet thread a sign of redemption through the blood of Christ.
Fourth, the family tree. Matthew's Gospel opens with Jesus's genealogy, and it names only a few women. Rahab is one: "Salmon begot Booz of Rahab," as the Douay-Rheims spells it.
She is the mother of Boaz, who will marry Ruth. A foreigner, a prostitute, in the line of King David, and of Jesus.

how: Catholics hear Rahab's name in the genealogy of Jesus from Matthew 1, read at the Christmas Vigil Mass and on December 17, and early Church writers such as Clement of Rome saw in her scarlet cord a sign of redemption through Christ's blood.

o: the woman of Jericho who hid Israel's two spies
a prophetess who judged Israel under a palm
the queen who ruled Jericho before Joshua came

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.

s: the Bible avoids saying what Rahab's work was
it says plainly she was a prostitute, and still names her in Jesus's family tree.
Rahab told the spies Jericho had been terrified of Israel
our hearts melted, she says, when we heard how the Lord dried up the sea.
Rahab is the only woman named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus
Matthew names a few: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, the wife of Uriah, and Mary.

games.q: you're Rahab. two Israelite spies are on your roof under the flax. the king's men are at your door demanding them. what do you do?
o: hand them over. it's the king's order.
say they left at dusk and send the soldiers the wrong way.
run and warn the rest of the city.
games.why: she says they left at dusk, sends the soldiers off toward the river, then goes up and tells the spies: the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on earth beneath.

practice: Think of someone you've filed away under a label: the neighbor with the messy past, the coworker everyone talks about, the relative who made bad choices. Ask what they might have risked that you never saw.
If you pray, pray for that person by name; if not, just let the label loosen for a minute.

wordCard.voice: Rahab. The woman of Jericho who hid the spies, tied a scarlet cord in her window, and is named among Jesus's ancestors. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a cord, and elsewhere in the Bible, hope. the scarlet line in Rahab's window (Joshua 2:18).

carryVoice: Your line: the scarlet cord. A thread in a window, a family safe. See you tomorrow.
